markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable extension: **SASRec with a gated recent-and-supported-history residual**, followed by a separate loss ablation. No benchmark improvement has been demonstrated; recurrence is a hypothesis requiring additional controls.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec attention can reflect repetition, but normalized pooling does not preserve absolute evidence counts. Similarity-weighted history therefore measures contextual support, not established recurring intent. (2) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings and a −0.4812 lower-tail margin. These motivate discrimination experiments without identifying their cause. (3) Embedding similarity near 0.54–0.56 provides little evidence of severe collapse, making strong diversity regularization a lower priority.

**Insights from related work.** (1) MSMT-LSI and SHAN motivate separating recent and historical preferences; HyperHawkes explicitly accumulates temporal triggering evidence. Its recurrence interpretation does not transfer automatically to normalized embedding pooling. (2) gSASRec and eSASRec motivate loss-only controls, with sampling policies documented precisely. (3) Graph projections motivate directed transition evidence, which cannot establish equipment compatibility.

**Framework.** Organize experiments along intent representation, ranking supervision, and transition evidence. SASRec remains the backbone; gated pooling changes representation, sampled softmax changes supervision, and a sparse transition residual changes evidence. Within pooling, distinguish recent evidence, older contextual support, and absolute support counts. Test components independently before combining them.

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a benefit and limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gated recent/history residual | 3: compact combination; established pooling | 7: useful platform; recurrence unproven | 8: targets stale influence and broad matches; cannot verify compatibility | 7: focused contexts; margin gains uncertain | 4: small modules; masking and serving integration |
| 128-negative sampled softmax | 2: established; little novelty | 8: strong control; sampler-sensitive | 5: discrimination; no explicit intent attribution | 9: targets confusion; false negatives persist | 3: compact loss; memory overhead |
| Directed transition residual | 5: distinct evidence; known approach | 7: interpretable; sparse transitions | 7: plausible next choices; associations mislead | 6: additional signal; popularity confounding | 5: sparse graph; serving integration |

**Selected algorithm.** Retain the original full-history pooling residual, renamed to avoid claiming recurrence. Recent pooling targets **older incidental influence**; recent-conditioned historical pooling targets **broad relevance crowding out specific current matches**. Better contextual discrimination targets Electronics’ weak margins. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated benefits.

Keep baseline loss initially. Compare baseline, residual-only, and loss-only models; prioritize a matched recent-only residual control. Then isolate disjoint older support and compare occurrence versus deduplicated pooling. Hold recent context fixed when removing or duplicating older support; control recency, popularity, parameter count, residual scale, and tuning effort. Only incremental older-history benefit supports a recurrence interpretation.

Select by unchanged macro validation HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives. Track category scores, margins, GPU cost, and all trials. Paired within-category bootstrap intervals are exploratory and conditional on selection; they do not remove winner’s optimism or establish full-catalog superiority.

idea.description: Extend each category’s SASRec with a gated residual combining the last five interactions and historical interactions similar to that recent context. Preserve the original full-prefix pooling as the primary proposal, but describe it as contextual support rather than a count-preserving recurrence mechanism. Keep candidate scoring as a dot product with trained item embeddings.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies older or incidental interactions receiving excessive influence and broad relatedness crowding out specific current matches. Recent pooling provides an explicit local signal, while recent-conditioned historical pooling may recover supporting interests. These mechanisms explicitly address two user-facing failures, although their effects require validation. Electronics’ negative lower-tail margin motivates testing contextual discrimination. Normalized attention can represent relative multiplicity but loses absolute count scale when all evidence is duplicated; the proposed residual alone does not establish recurring intent. Histories also cannot establish purchase satisfaction, functional compatibility, or why preferences changed.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use only training histories and learned item embeddings. Review text, ratings, item categories, prices, stores, and simulator traits are unavailable; never fabricate them. Titles, descriptions, and timestamps are permitted but unnecessary for this initial experiment. Preserve all four category routes, baseline splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Keep execution single-GPU and account for every training, diagnostic, failed trial, and checkpoint evaluation within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

Inherit baseline architecture settings, optimizer, batch construction, sequence length, and loss unchanged for the representation comparison; serialize their resolved values. Honor SASREC_EPOCHS, whose host default is 200. Use recent window 5, cosine temperature 0.2, a bias-free Linear(2D,D) residual projection, and a scalar gate_logit initialized to -4. Initialize projection weights normally using the baseline initialization convention. Keep the embedding padding row zero and explicitly mask embeddings, pooled contexts, and final outputs at padded queries. Compute recent means with prefix cumulative sums and counts over positions t−4 through t. Use epsilon-safe normalization, causal key masks, and finite handling of empty rows before softmax. Vectorized historical pooling costs O(BL²D), with O(BL²) attention storage; vectorization does not make it linear.

Save the complete module, configuration, and category routing, and update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the identical architecture. Its full-catalog unseen-item scoring must use the same fused representation and scoring function. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must reference the complete trained model; item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data retain their interfaces. Existing margin and embedding probes remain applicable. Category breakdowns must explicitly report unavailable metadata rather than invent categories. A B×L sampled-negative probe measures that diagnostic sampler, not the entire multi-negative training objective or validation HR@10.

Prespecify baseline, residual-only, and loss-only comparisons before inspecting their validation results. Use the baseline checkpoint evaluation schedule unchanged and record it; choose the highest pinned macro validation HR@10, breaking checkpoint ties toward the earlier epoch and model ties toward unchanged SASRec. Do not tune per-category architectures independently in this initial comparison. Bound the planned runs using recorded baseline GPU costs, and log all configurations, checkpoint evaluations, failures, and GPU seconds. If budget permits mechanistic controls, prioritize an equally parameterized recent-only residual, then disjoint older-history pooling, then occurrence versus deduplicated pooling. Use a bias-free shared projection and the same gate settings; report residual RMS and include a scale-matched sensitivity analysis. Deduplicating IDs tests item multiplicity, not recurrence among distinct but related items. A frequency-weighted mean preserves relative counts, while a sum or explicit count feature changes absolute evidence scale and requires a separate, capacity- and scale-controlled proposal. Do not silently add such a mechanism to the selected model.

For the separate loss trial, retain unchanged SASRec and use 128 catalogue-uniform negatives per positive, sampled with replacement from nonpadding items. Mask draws matching that position’s target; retain other duplicates and history collisions, documenting this exact policy. Compute uncorrected sampled-softmax cross-entropy over the positive and remaining sampled logits. This is a sampled classification objective, not an unbiased full-softmax estimator; do not add an unjustified negative-only logQ correction. A gBCE alternative would require its own trial: the supplied official recommendation is K=256 and t=0.75, alpha=K/(catalogue_size−1), beta=1−t+alpha*t. Its official sampler permits collisions, so rejection would be an explicit deviation. These alternatives do not establish that harder negatives are needed.

Where pinned evaluator outputs permit, retain paired per-user hits for prespecified comparisons. Bootstrap 200 users with replacement independently within each category, preserving model pairing; use 10,000 CPU resamples with a fixed recorded seed, and report the macro difference, percentile 95% interval, category differences, and win/loss counts. One changed hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Optional exact McNemar tests assess discordant hits. Intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on candidates, training seeds, and searched models; they do not correct adaptive selection. Cached-prediction out-of-bag checkpoint analyses are exploratory, and extra training seeds measure training variability rather than independent confirmation. Freeze the full procedure before the host’s untouched final evaluation. Preserve the host evaluator throughout; sampled-candidate gains do not establish full-catalog usefulness. No execution or measured improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
# Baseline architecture, splits, routing, optimizer, and loss are inherited unchanged.
# All tensor operations below are batched; sequence has shape B x L.
class InterestResidualSASRec:
    def __init__(self, baseline, D):
        self.sasrec = baseline
        self.item_emb = baseline.item_emb
        self.projection = Linear(2 * D, D, bias=False)
        self.gate_logit = Parameter(-4.0)
        # Initialize projection normally; do not zero both gate and branch.

    def log2feats(self, sequence):
        valid = sequence != 0
        base = self.sasrec.log2feats(sequence)
        emb = self.item_emb(sequence) * valid[..., None]
        recent = causal_window_mean_from_prefix_sums(
            emb, valid, window=5, denominator_clamp=1)
        query = normalize(recent, eps=1e-8)
        key = normalize(emb, eps=1e-8)
        logits = batched_matmul(query, transpose(key)) / 0.2
        allowed = causal_mask(L) & valid[:, None, :]
        nonempty = allowed.any(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        logits = logits.masked_fill(~allowed, -inf)
        logits = where(nonempty, logits, zeros_like(logits))
        weights = softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        weights = weights.masked_fill(~allowed, 0)
        weights = weights / weights.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-8)
        supported = batched_matmul(weights, emb)
        residual = self.projection(concat(recent, supported, dim=-1))
        fused = base + sigmoid(self.gate_logit) * residual
        return fused * valid[..., None]

    def predict_score(self, features, items):
        return dot(features, self.item_emb(items))

# Primary trials, using the same resolved baseline settings and pinned evaluator:
# A: unchanged SASRec, unchanged loss.
# B: residual SASRec, unchanged loss.
# C: unchanged SASRec, 128-negative sampled-softmax objective.
# Do not combine B and C before independent comparisons.
# If budget permits, compare B against matched recent-only and older-only controls.
# Older-only pooling excludes every position in the recent window; empty support = 0.
# Remove/duplicate older support with the recent context fixed for mechanism probes.
# Select by pinned macro HR@10; preserve all four category routes.
# Serialize configuration and complete parameters; emit the matching predictor.

originality.positive: The residual offers a compact, testable combination of recent context and contextual historical support within the existing SASRec interface.
originality.negative: Long- and short-term attention fusion is established, and normalized support pooling does not introduce a new recurrence mechanism.

future_potential.positive: Controlled comparisons can reveal whether explicit local context or older support helps, providing a foundation for later timestamp-aware or count-sensitive models.
future_potential.negative: Self-reinforcing embedding similarity, overlap between recent and historical branches, and unavailable compatibility evidence limit interpretation and generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: The learned addition is small: one projection, one scalar gate, and vectorized pooling, with unchanged dot-product scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct causal masking, padding behavior, quadratic attention memory, diagnostic adaptation, predictor serialization, and matched controls require careful integration.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention backbone and item-embedding scoring.
Normalized attention can assign greater relative mass to repeated evidence.
limitations: Does not explicitly preserve absolute support counts; positional encodings complicate simple duplication-invariance arguments.
Its architecture alone does not establish why observed recommendations miss current intent.

related_work.title: MSMT-LSI
contributions: Uses separate long- and short-term attention networks with temporal embeddings.
limitations: Its reported setting does not establish gains on the pinned RecHarness benchmark.

related_work.title: HyperHawkes
contributions: Combines latent intent discovery, recurring-interest modeling, and immediate-interest attention.
Temporal Hawkes triggering sums historical contributions, preserving cumulative support subject to temporal kernels.
limitations: A full recurrence model adds complexity beyond the proposed initial residual.
Its recurring latent intents are not equivalent to repeated item IDs or normalized embedding-similarity pooling.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates correcting negative-sampling-induced overconfidence and evaluating multiple negatives.
The supplied official implementation recommends 256 negatives and gBCE calibration t=0.75.
limitations: Does not establish the cause of Electronics’ observed ranking errors.
The official catalogue-uniform replacement sampler permits collisions; collision rejection changes its sampling policy.

related_work.title: eSASRec
contributions: Supports testing sampled softmax with autoregressive sequential recommendation.
Studies improved Transformer layers and multiple negative-sampling configurations.
limitations: A loss change alone does not explicitly address stale or incidental interest attribution.
Sampling corrections must reflect the actual sampler and deterministic positive inclusion.

related_work.title: Revisiting Graph Projections
contributions: Motivates a lightweight directed transition channel constructed from interaction histories.
limitations: Observed transitions do not verify complementarity, prerequisites, or equipment compatibility.

related_work.title: Sequential Recommendation with User Memory Networks (SHAN)
contributions: Pools long-term items using user-conditioned attention, then combines that representation with short-term items through attention.
Provides a direct precedent for hierarchical long- and short-term preference fusion.
limitations: Normalized pooling does not explicitly preserve absolute evidence counts.
Its results do not validate this residual on the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides a reference for paired bootstrap comparison.
limitations: Within-category paired resampling for macro HR@10 is an application of the method, not a reported recommendation experiment.
Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive model selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how model selection can overfit finite validation estimates and bias reported performance.
limitations: Does not provide an automatic correction for this task’s adaptive architecture search.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog model rankings.
limitations: Does not change the required benchmark objective or establish which candidate model will perform best here.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Distinguishes sampling corrections that account for deterministic positive inclusion from naive candidate corrections.
limitations: Sampling-bias correction does not identify false negatives.
Changing collision rejection or sampling proposals requires rederiving applicable expected counts.

related_work.title: PyTorch Transformer Building Blocks
contributions: Provides engineering context for attention masks and fully masked attention rows.
limitations: The proposed safe pooling implementation is an engineering adaptation, not evidence of recommendation gains.
